state: v15 uses the word bare in every section, and its own keyfigure block leads with the collision: 82,265 installs of the extension that owns the name (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:13).

path: Round r7 measured the collision on 2026-08-28 and rated it MEDIUM-HIGH, HIGH if shipped bare (e6-naming-risk.md:10).

The SEO half of the case is worth nothing this year, because nothing in the plan is a search channel. A rename bought on search grounds buys a channel we do not use.
Today's competitor sweep moves the collision closer. If distribution runs through the git-backed CMS shelf, the incumbent is a shelf neighbour as well as a name neighbour.

recCase: The identifier and the marketing name do not have to match, and making them match is what turns a naming decision into a migration.
One string in the build plan is declared unchangeable and it points at an unchecked domain. That is the single fixable mistake here, and it is one line (docs/DEV-PLAN.md:627).
The publishing wildcard is the second, because customers point their own DNS at it (docs/DEV-PLAN.md:1683).
Leaving `ai.sgnk.md` is worse than either alternative, because it writes another product's identity into a notarised bundle.
questions.flip: If the name is frozen this week under N2, the identifier and the brand can be the same string and (a) is simpler.

questions.q: Do we contact the incumbent's author before deciding the name, and when?
questions.lede: He has publicly asked for company collaboration, the email has been on our open list since 2026-08-28, and nobody has sent it.

items.label: Front Matter CMS created
items.note: senior use in the same trade channel

visual.note: He holds three "Front Matter" listings in the store an extension would ship into.
visual.caption: An open door, logged and not walked through

questions.stakes: An email cannot be unsent, and if a mark exists it changes what that email means.
state: No approach has been made. The r7 report read his README and found a "2026 Open Source Priorities Update" (e6-naming-risk.md:52; x4-external-frontier-importer-naming.md:141).
In it, open source "isn't providing me a sustainable income", the project stays maintained, and major changes need "a company commitment" (e6-naming-risk.md:52).
The master plan logged it the day it was found, as "F6 (new) the detente email to Elio Struyf" (FRONTMATTER-MASTER-PLAN-2026-08-28.md:182).
The plan's rule for outbound acts is explicit: "A maintainer PR is outbound; approval first" (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:305).
path: The r7 report called the priorities update "a concrete detente/partnership/brand-acquisition opening" (e6-naming-risk.md:52).
The same report found no trade-mark symbol and no enforcement posture anywhere, and concluded confusion rather than legal cost is the binding constraint (e6-naming-risk.md:89).
That conclusion is tagged as inference and was built from searches that could not open a single register (e6-naming-risk.md:84).
tension: Contacting creates a dated written record that we knew about the collision before shipping, which is the fact a passing-off argument wants.
Not contacting leaves a 2019 senior user unmanaged, holding three "Front Matter" listings in the store an extension would ship into (e6-naming-risk.md:87).
Today's research makes him nearer, not further. Git-backed markdown CMS tools are the adjacency being considered as distribution, and his product is one.

recCase: The corpus reads confusion rather than litigation as the binding constraint, but that read is tagged inference and was built from searches that opened no register (e6-naming-risk.md:84, :89).
One EU mark has been reported and never reproduced, and if it exists the email means something different (docs/GAPS-2026-09-08.md:146).
N3's free searches cost an hour, so the delay is a week at most.
Outbound acts need approval under the plan's own rule, so this is a founder send either way (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:305).

questions.stakes: The name gets settled on registry probes and taste, with no evidence from anyone who is not us.
state: Weeks 1-2 run four tests across fifteen recruited people plus 20 team conversations (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:352).
The tested variable is three headline variants (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:296). The name is not a variable in any test.
There is already a five-second screenshot test in the script, asking what the blue tint means (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:411).
§64.6 scores two names against six criteria; four are pure judgment and the other two rest on registry probes (r13-s4-positioning-messaging.md:129-136).
path: The tests were designed around the headline, because the headline is what the 2026-09-08 adversarial round attacked and did not leave standing (docs/GAPS-2026-09-08.md:124).
Round r11 generated 41 candidates and pruned to 15 on handle availability alone (r4-naming-candidates.md:29, :63).
No record anywhere in the corpus shows a candidate name being read by a person outside the project (searched 2026-09-09).
tension: Recruiting is already happening and the question costs ten seconds a person.
A landing-page arm would read the name cleanly, but the arms are what the two weeks exist to settle (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:296).
Five people is a weak signal and must never be reported as more than that.
If N2 freezes the name before week 1, asking becomes a post-hoc justification rather than evidence.

recCase: The test is already recruiting fifteen people and the question takes ten seconds, so it is the cheapest evidence available on a decision that has none.
Separate landing pages would spend a headline arm on a naming question, and the headline arms are the reason the two weeks exist (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:296).
The script already contains a five-second recognition test, so the format is proven within this study (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:411).
questions.flip: If the name is frozen before week 1 under N2, drop the question rather than run it for comfort.

merged.why: N8's real question was whether the SEO argument counts in the name decision, and its options collapsed into N1's (accept the ceiling / coin / domain-as-brand). Its evidence is carried whole.
Both are timing. N10 asked whether the name precedes the form factor; N2 asks when the name stops being changeable. One sitting answers both, and N2's recommendation now sets the order.
Same option set: bind a string to the brand, bind it to something name-free, or defer. The bundle identifier and the permanent URIs are the same decision seen twice.

notes: 11 to 8, a 27% cut, inside the contract's 15-35% band. I stopped at 8 rather than forcing 7: the remaining pairs (N3 clearance and N9 the incumbent; N4 two names and N1 the word) have genuinely different option sets, and merging them would have destroyed a decision rather than tidied one. Two corrections to facts the old cards carried: (1) N1 and N11 both said 41 candidate names were 61 — r4-naming-candidates.md:29 reads "41 names, with strategy", and the availability table at :63 is "top 15", so 41 and 15 are the real figures; the wrong number is called out inside the evidence row so it is not quietly restated. (2) N1's problem field cited section 52.3's rank-1 form without a line; it is 22-segments-disclosure-naming.md:219 (`frontmatterapp`), and the prohibition it contradicts is :223, with the falsifier at :225 — all three now cited individually. Every file:line in this file was read with sed before it was written. Three claims from today's briefing were added and are flagged in the prose as coming from the 2026-09-09 round, not from the corpus: the working-tree diff is now free in four editors (weakens the extension route independently of the name), git-backed markdown CMS tools are being weighed as a distribution shelf (which makes Front Matter CMS a shelf neighbour, not only a name neighbour), and nothing in the briefing changes the collision measurements themselves. No briefing figure was used in any diagram; the only funnel in the area uses corpus numbers 41/15/2/0.
